note: Batch 24 atomically retires S26 (steward-write.ts:279, resolveEmployeeStewardSourceWorkspaceDir) and S27 (steward-write.ts:280, resolveEmployeeStewardTargetWorkspaceDir), the last two live steward host-path resolver call sites, taking the accepted baseline from 12 to a proposed 10. It resolves the Batch 23 Semantic Gate finding: S26/S27 sit inside runEmployeeStewardCutoverPilot, a provisioning/create lifecycle where the source/target bindings did not pre-exist at the call site, so a read-existing-binding resolver swap was circular. The honest remediation, the narrow domain command provisionEmployeeStewardCutoverWorkspace (implemented and accepted in #679, present in base 3db1aa85d0), is now wired in: the test-only pilot moved to provision-steward-cutover.ts, accepts trusted caller-supplied placement (sourceRoot/targetRoot), and calls the command to create the unique source canonical/active binding and the unique target compatibility/read_only binding (Catalog-first, fencing operation + receipt, mkdir/copy only after Catalog success). S26 then reads the source canonical binding locator and S27 reads the target compatibility/read_only binding locator from that Catalog; the host-path resolvers are no longer called in production code. Two now-unused imports (advanceCutoverOperation, createWorkspaceCutoverOperation) were removed from steward-write.ts. Neighbour S24 (line 150, resolveWorkspaceLocator) and S25 (line 151, resolveWorkspaceTargetBinding) keep their accepted posture; their tests were re-anchored to the site content (const sourceRoot / const targetRoot) instead of brittle absolute line numbers because the import removal shifted lines. The Phase 0 freeze scanner stays ok=true with addedProductionCallSites=[] (no new frozen calls sneaked in). Placement is a trusted input validated by the command (absolute, no traversal, source != target); missing/duplicate bindings, cross-tenant access, path escape, and receipt failure all fail closed with no host fallback, no partial binding, no partial directory, and no double write. No production Catalog write, no schema v2, no LIVE, no delete of old data; item 7 stays not-met; Phase 1B execution stays blocked; deploy stays unauthorized. proposedRemaining=10 is now the canonical accepted baseline: on 2026-08-25 the independent reviewer (kiro-sot-reviewer) accepted Batch 24 via CR1 re-verification after the pilot test-only boundary machine gate landed (#720), so batch24Accepted=true and lastAcceptedRetirementBaseline is canonicalized 12->10. If any part of S26 or S27 had failed, the baseline would remain 12 and would not be decremented to 11 or 10. This acceptance updates ONLY the Item 7 accepted retirement baseline (12->10); it explicitly does NOT grant Stage C unlock, Item 7 met, Phase 1B unlock, production deployment, or LIVE. deployAuthorized stays false and live stays forbidden until Item 7 reaches 0, I3 is executed, a Phase 1B unlock receipt is issued, and the production candidate passes forward-only and delivery alignment.
